Act') and was sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for 03 months and to pay a fine of `500/- for commission of the offences, for which he . was convicted. 2. The case of the prosecution was that on 22.4.2004 Food Inspector L.D. Thakur inspected the premises i.e. Chanchal Singh Sweets Shop, Rohru at about 10:00 a.m. and found the present petitioner conducting business of said sweet shop. The of items which were kept for sale to the general public included "burfi, mutter, besan burfi, namkeen" etc. Food Inspector asked rt the petitioner to produce P.F.A. licence issued in his favour for sale of food articles, as was required under Rule 50 of P.F.A. Rules, 1955, however, accused failed to produce any licence issued in his favour to conduct the abovementioned business for the years 2003-2005. Besides this, the sweets were kept uncovered exposed to rain, dust and flies. Accordingly, Food Inspector prepared a spot map which was duly signed by the accused and Food Inspector himself. Thereafter, Food Inspector placed documents of the accused before Chief Medical Officer, Shimla who was empowered to give written consent under Section 20 of the P.F.A. Act to launch prosecution against the accused. In this background, Food Inspector filed complaint against the accused under Section 16(1)(a)(ii) of P.F.A. Act. 3. As a prima facie case was made out against the accused for commission of offence punishable under Section 16(1)(a)(II) read with Section 7(iii) of P.F.A. Act, 1954, accordingly notice of accusation was put to him to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 6. Feeling aggrieved by the said two judgments passed by learned courts below, the accused has preferred the present revision petition.
texts.arguments: Even during the course of arguments, learned counsel for the petitioner could not point out as to what was the perversity with the findings returned by both learned courts below or which particular finding returned either by learned trial court or by learned appellate court was not borne . Lastly it was argued by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner has suffered pain and agony of trial for more than 12 years and it was prayed that keeping in view the fact that the petitioner is 65 years of age as of now, the of sentence of imprisonment of the petitioner be commuted to fine and in this regard reliance was placed by the learned counsel for rt the petitioner on the following decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court:- (i) In Haripada Das v. State of West Bangal and another, 1998 (2) FAC 187, the Apex Curt has held:- "Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also considering that the appellant was released on bail by this Court long back and because of the protracted litigation up to this court he has also suffered a lot of mental agony and also financial hardship and also considering the fact that he had already undergone imprisonment for more than three weeks, we feel that in the facts of the case the ends of the justice will be met if the sentence of imprisonment is reduced to the period already undergone. (ii) N. Sukumaran Nair v. Food Inspector Navelikara, 1996 Vol. 2 PFA Case 21 wherein it was held:- "The offence took place in the year 1984. Under clause (d) of Section 433 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the appropriate government is empowered to commute the sentence of simple imprisonment for fine. On deposit of such fine, the State Government may formalize he matter by passing appropriate orders under clause (d) of Section 433 of the code of Criminal Procedure." (iii) Santosh Kumar v.
